text:
Silo 

 
 A self-hosted media server for films, series, audiobooks, ebooks, podcasts, and manga.
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 Quick start 
 · Documentation 
 · Builds & releases 
 · Discord 
 · Support Silo 
 · Contributing 
 

---

 [!WARNING]
 Silo is pre-release. APIs, configuration, and database migrations may change
 before the first stable release. Back up your deployment before updating.

 1.0 release scope

The 1.0 milestone covers movies and
series. Audiobooks, ebooks, and Audiobookshelf compatibility keep working as
they do today and are labeled beta : they are outside the 1.0 support
promise and will be replaced by a consolidated Books effort with no assigned
release date. The broader capabilities below include those beta
implementations, not a promise that every media type is supported in 1.0.
Existing library data is preserved when upgrading.

 What Silo does

 
 
 
 Play 
 Direct play when possible, remux when needed, transcode otherwise, with
 VA-API, Quick Sync, and NVENC hardware acceleration.
 
 
 Organize 
 One catalog for films, series, audiobooks, ebooks, podcasts, and manga,
 matched through metadata plugins such as TMDB and TVDB.
 
 
 Connect 
 Use the included web app, or the Jellyfin/Emby-compatible API with clients
 such as VidHub ,
 Findroid , and
 Infuse . Client coverage varies.
 
 
 
 
 Share 
 Household profiles with their own watch state, library access, and
 parental controls.
 
 
 Manage 
 Libraries, users, providers, storage, search, and playback are configured
 in the admin interface, not in config files.
 
 
 Scale 
 Start with one integrated server; add transcode nodes that need only its
 URL and a key, or proxy nodes that share its PostgreSQL and Redis, when
 you need to.
 
 
 

 Quick start

Requires Docker Compose 2.24 or newer. The default Compose file runs the
omnibus image: Silo with a bundled PostgreSQL (with pgvector) and Redis, plus
Meilisearch when you turn it on.

 

Set MEDIA ROOT in .env to the absolute path of your media, then:

 

Open and complete onboarding.

Hardware transcoding (VA-API or NVIDIA) and PostgreSQL and Redis access for
proxy nodes on other hosts are commented out in docker-compose.yml ; uncomment
the lines you need. Transcode nodes reach the server on its web port.

 Updating an install from before the omnibus image

An install that runs Silo, PostgreSQL, and Redis in separate containers keeps
that layout when its .env sets COMPOSE FILE=docker-compose.advanced.yml ; set
it before updating. docker-compose.yml is an example of a new install and
does not look for an earlier one: started on that data folder, it replaces
the old silo container and comes up on a new, empty database with setup
open, while the earlier PostgreSQL and Redis keep running with their data
untouched. Moving into the single container is a separate step. The separate GPU and node Compose files are gone, so a COMPOSE FILE 
that names one fails until it names only the deployment file you use, with
the matching lines in it uncommented. See Moving from the multi-container
stack.

The user manual covers the rest, starting with
installation: backing up SECRET KEY ,
storage, GPU acceleration, Meilisearch, external PostgreSQL and Redis,
transcode nodes, PostgreSQL tuning, backups, and updates.

 Builds and releases

Until the first release, default-branch images carry an ordered build-N tag
and the full commit SHA alongside latest . Build numbers order published images;
they are not release versions. Release versioning
defines each tag and the SemVer contract.

 Documentation

- User manual — installing, configuring, and running Silo
- Development guide — source setup, builds, tests, migrations
- Settings API, Downloads API, and Apple Push Display Token — client contracts

 Community and contributions

Questions and discussion: Discord.
Bugs, install problems, and performance issues: the
GitHub issue forms,
which ask for reproduction steps and raw logs.

Native clients are developed in
 silo-apple and
 silo-android . Client-visible
API, authentication, playback, or metadata changes should consider both.

Right now, the most helpful way to contribute is a clear, accurate issue. We
implement and review changes through our own workflow, and pull request volume
has outgrown what we can review carefully, so a good issue usually helps us
more than a pull request.

Feature ideas go in
Discussions → Ideas,
not issues.

Pull requests are still welcome from contributors who've had one merged in a
Silo repository, or when a maintainer asks for one; a feature pull request also
needs an issue in this repository that a maintainer has labeled accepted .
Other pull requests are closed automatically without review; when a maintainer
asked for one, they reopen it. CONTRIBUTING.md explains what
makes an issue useful.

 Supporting Silo

Silo is free and open source, and it will stay that way. It's built in spare
time and paid for out of pocket.

 
 
 

Sponsorship pays for AI development tooling (Claude, Codex), the
push-notification relay, and future project costs. You can help just as much
without spending anything:

- Report bugs with steps to reproduce on
 GitHub Issues.
- Help other users on Discord.
- Improve the docs at siloserver.org.
- Contribute code by following CONTRIBUTING.md.

 Sponsors

 
 
 
 
 
 Code review is supported by Macroscope through its open source program. 
 

 License and trademarks

Silo's source code is licensed under the

an additional permission to combine it with platform SDKs such as the Windows
App SDK. See LICENSE and PLATFORM-EXCEPTION.md.

The Silo name, logo, and wordmark are trademarks of Silo Media L.L.C. and
are not covered by the AGPL. Forks and redistributions may use the code but must
not use the Silo brand as their identity and must remove or replace the brand
assets. Publishing a Silo-branded app to an app store requires written

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
Requires Docker Compose 2.24 or newer. The default Compose file runs the omnibus image: Silo with a bundled PostgreSQL (with pgvector) and Redis, plus Meilisearch when you turn it on.

git clone https://github.com/Silo-Server/silo-server.git
cd silo-server
cp .env.example .env
chmod 600 .env
key="$(openssl rand -base64 48)" && printf '\nSECRET_KEY=%s\n' "$key" >> .env

Set MEDIA_ROOT in .env to the absolute path of your media, then:

docker compose up -d

Open http://localhost:8090 and complete onboarding.

Hardware transcoding (VA-API or NVIDIA) and PostgreSQL and Redis access for proxy nodes on other hosts are commented out in docker-compose.yml; uncomment the lines you need. Transcode nodes reach the server on its web port.

Updating an install from before the omnibus image

An install that runs Silo, PostgreSQL, and Redis in separate containers keeps that layout when its .env sets COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.advanced.yml; set it before updating. docker-compose.yml is an example of a new install and does not look for an earlier one: started on that data folder, it replaces the old silo container and comes up on a new, empty database with setup open, while the earlier PostgreSQL and Redis keep running with their data untouched. Moving into the single container is a separate step. The separate GPU and node Compose files are gone, so a COMPOSE_FILE that names one fails until it names only the deployment file you use, with the matching lines in it uncommented. See Moving from the multi-container stack.

The user manual covers the rest, starting with installation: backing up SECRET_KEY, storage, GPU acceleration, Meilisearch, external PostgreSQL and Redis, transcode nodes, PostgreSQL tuning, backups, and updates.
